ci: Use one network per container and rm it after success

The networks were left around for the next run, which may cause issues
when they are changed in a future CI change.

Fix it by using one network per container, and by cleaning it up after a
successful run.

This also allows to harden the script by removing the check=False on
creation.

On a failed run, networks will remain dangling and need manual pruning
(same behaviour as before).

util: cap Sock::WaitMany timeout

bitcoin-cli turns -rpcclienttimeout=0 into a 5 year timeout and passes
it down to Sock::Wait. On systems without poll() (e.g. macOS and the
BSDs) the wait is done with select(), which fails with EINVAL for
timeouts above 10^8 seconds on macOS. So since the libevent removal in
34342, `bitcoin-cli -rpcclienttimeout=0 ...` fails on macOS with
"Could not connect to the server". With poll(), the millisecond count
is narrowed to int, so large values can wrap as well.

Cap the timeout at INT_MAX milliseconds (about 24.8 days), which fits
poll() and stays below the 31 days that POSIX requires select() to
accept.

Add a bitcoin-cli call with -rpcclienttimeout=0 to
interface_bitcoin_cli.py. It fails on macOS without the cap.

util: cap Sock::WaitMany timeout

bitcoin-cli turns -rpcclienttimeout=0 into a 5 year timeout and passes
it down to Sock::Wait. On systems without poll() (e.g. macOS and the
BSDs) the wait is done with select(), which fails with EINVAL for
timeouts above 10^8 seconds on macOS. So since the libevent removal in
34342, `bitcoin-cli -rpcclienttimeout=0 ...` fails on macOS with
"Could not connect to the server". With poll(), the millisecond count
is narrowed to int, so large values can wrap as well.

Cap the timeout at INT_MAX milliseconds (about 24.8 days), which fits
poll() and stays below the 31 days that POSIX requires select() to
accept.

Add a bitcoin-cli call with -rpcclienttimeout=0 to
interface_bitcoin_cli.py. It fails on macOS without the cap.

test: Extract and use sigterm_node in init_fd_overflow_test

Changes:

* Extract a shared get_process_group_kwargs() to avoid repeating it
* In sigterm_node, use node.wait_until_stopped() instead of the manual
  assert_equal(0, node.process.wait())
* Extract sigterm_node; can be reviewed via the git options
  --color-moved=dimmed-zebra --color-moved-ws=ignore-all-space
* Use self.sigterm_node(node)+get_process_group_kwargs() over
  node.kill_process() for a graceful shutdown to avoid complaints from
  the llvm-symbolizer about a broken pipe when it resolves UBSAN
  suppressions during a process kill
